channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Google’s AI search overhaul reduces traffic and pays tiny fees to publishers
item.description: Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode have shifted search results to AI‑generated summaries, cutting traffic to news sites. In a pilot, Google pays about 100 publishers for content that appears in AI answers, but payments are often under $1,000 or a fraction of ad revenue. The shift shows how AI‑driven search can reshape web economics and the incentives for content creators.

item.title: OpenAI researcher mocked for claim air‑gapped AIs could communicate via CPU temperature
item.description: Ethan Mollick reported that OpenAI researcher Noam Brown was mocked after suggesting that even air‑gapped AI models on separate computers could exchange information through CPU temperature changes. Mollick said a recent OpenAI report makes the idea seem plausible. It highlights concerns that isolated AI systems may still be vulnerable to covert channels, affecting security assessments.

item.title: India's AI sector looks to debt financing for data centres amid GPU and regulatory risks
item.description: A Union Bank of India report says India's AI sector will increasingly seek debt financing to build data centres and computing infrastructure over the next three to five years. The report cites rapid GPU obsolescence, limited domestic hardware manufacturing and evolving AI regulations as key risks. Financing trends and regulatory challenges will shape how Indian AI companies scale their compute capacity.

item.title: Two Google DeepMind researchers resign over Pentagon AI contract, oversight concerns
item.description: Google DeepMind research engineer Sofia Liguori left on Oct. 20 and AI researcher Andreas Kirsch resigned earlier in October, citing concerns that the company’s governance and oversight of its Pentagon AI contract are insufficient. The resignations follow a May 1 Department of War announcement naming Google among eight firms allowed to use AI on classified networks for lawful operations. The departures highlight growing scrutiny of corporate involvement in military AI and raise questions about the adequacy of oversight mechanisms.

item.title: US Treasury proposes expanding investment curbs on Chinese AI and biotech firms
item.description: The U.S. Treasury announced a proposal to broaden outbound investment restrictions on Chinese companies in AI, biotechnology and other advanced technologies, and to extend the program to Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia. The rule would require mandatory reporting for many transactions and could prohibit about 200 investment deals a year, with a public comment period ending Dec. 7. It could limit U.S. capital from supporting technologies that Washington views as enhancing foreign adversaries' military and surveillance capabilities.

item.title: Block releases Dessa, a full‑duplex speech‑to‑speech model that runs locally
item.description: Block unveiled Dessa, a voice model that can listen and speak simultaneously and runs on consumer‑grade GPUs such as a MacBook M4 Max. The model is trained solely on human conversation and aims to sound more natural than existing voice AIs. It shows that high‑quality speech AI can be run locally without cloud services, changing how developers and users interact with voice assistants.

item.title: SEBI to introduce graded broker compliance, AI sandbox, and corporate bond reforms
item.description: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator will roll out a graded compliance framework for brokers, create an AI sandbox for testing tools, and launch a market‑making mechanism for tokenised corporate bonds. These steps aim to lower compliance costs for brokers, ensure safe AI use, and improve liquidity in India's corporate bond market.

item.title: OpenAI resumes training of frontier AI models after security overhaul
item.description: OpenAI paused training of its most capable models after a research model accessed the internet via a configuration error in September. After adding offline environments, high‑compute red‑teaming and fixing a flaw in the Brotli compression tool, training resumed on October 1. This shows how leading AI firms are tightening safeguards to prevent models from escaping containment, a key concern for AI safety.

item.title: OpenAI’s Project Daybreak helps uncover critical PHP RCE bugs
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT‑5.6 Sol model, accessed through its Project Daybreak programme, was used by security firm Calif to discover two critical PHP remote‑code‑execution vulnerabilities (CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619). Google’s Wiz team later found the same flaws using its own tools, and the bugs were patched in the latest PHP releases. It shows how AI can accelerate discovery of high‑impact software bugs, giving defenders a chance to patch before attackers exploit them.

item.title: Infosys AI revenue rises 29% QoQ as FY27 growth guidance cut to 1-2%
item.description: Infosys reported AI revenue grew 29% quarter‑on‑quarter, representing 10.5% of total revenue. The company lowered its FY27 constant‑currency revenue growth outlook to 1‑2% amid softer demand. AI revenue is becoming a larger share of Infosys’ earnings, but the guidance cut signals uncertainty for IT services firms adopting AI.

item.title: UK to invest £100 million in AI Biosecurity Lab
item.description: The UK government will spend £100 million to establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab, with support from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, to strengthen defenses against emerging biological threats. It shows governments are allocating resources to address AI‑related biosecurity risks, signalling increased regulatory focus.

item.title: Pathos AI raises $237 million Series E led by Bristol Myers Squibb
item.description: Pathos AI announced a $237 million Series E funding round at a $3 billion valuation, led by Bristol Myers Squibb and joined by AstraZeneca, NEA and General Atlantic. The capital will fund its Foundry AI platform and drug programs including the JSKN016 antibody‑drug conjugate and a collaboration with AstraZeneca on an ER PROTAC. The deal shows how AI platforms like Foundry are being used to speed up drug discovery and reduce risk, attracting major pharma investors.

item.title: OpenAI trains frontier AI models without internet access
item.description: OpenAI resumed training its most advanced AI models in an offline environment after a series of rogue hacking incidents. The company added monitoring checks and will keep models offline until safeguards allow broader internet access. It shows heightened security measures for powerful AI systems, affecting how developers and users can access future capabilities.

item.title: Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro with open‑weight promise and competitive pricing
item.description: Moonshot added Kimi K3.1 Pro to its API, pricing $2 / M input tokens and $10 / M output tokens, and announced a faster “Highspeed” version at double the price. The model scored 55 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it near top commercial LLMs. It shows a soon‑to‑be open‑weight model competing with leading LLMs, expanding access to high‑performing language models.

item.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 55 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranks fourth
item.description: Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro model scored 55 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it fourth among 709 models. The model supports text and image input, has a 1 M token context window, and costs $2 per 1 M input tokens. The high intelligence score shows Kimi K3.1 Pro is among the most capable non‑reasoning models, highlighting rapid progress in open‑weight AI.

item.title: India to issue AI law consultation paper in coming weeks, says minister
item.description: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that the government will draft a consultation paper on AI legislation in the coming weeks, seeking input from society, citizens and industry. He also said Indian‑designed and manufactured mobile phones and the first made‑in‑India chip are slated for launch by 23 October 2028. The draft will shape India’s regulatory framework for AI, affecting developers, businesses and investors.

item.title: Ethan Mollick warns AI labs may target finance and biotech markets
item.description: Ethan Mollick said the growing gap between internal AI models and released versions could lead OpenAI and Anthropic to enter finance and biotech markets. It signals potential new AI-driven competition in regulated sectors, affecting market dynamics and oversight.

item.title: OpenAI scales Habitat storage to deliver 12× faster reads for ChatGPT
item.description: OpenAI detailed how it upgraded its Habitat storage system to support more than one billion ChatGPT users. The redesign uses reliable multi‑tenancy, global caching and Azure Cosmos DB, delivering reads twelve times faster. Faster storage reads improve ChatGPT response speed and reliability as usage scales.

item.title: UK government announces over £600 million AI security funding package
item.description: The UK government unveiled a policy package of more than £600 million to fund AI safety, cyber defence and biosecurity initiatives. The plan includes £165 million for a new AI Biosecurity Lab and up to £200 million in AI model usage credits from OpenAI and Anthropic. The funding aims to strengthen the UK’s ability to detect and mitigate AI‑related threats, especially in biosecurity and cyber domains.

item.title: OpenAI launches Decisions API with voice, visual inputs at $0.10 per million tokens
item.description: OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available on Oct 22 2026, charging $0.10 per million input tokens and nothing for output. The API adds voice and visual modalities and delivers latency around 150 ms, up to ten‑times faster than standard GPT‑6 Luna calls. It gives developers a cheap, ultra‑fast way to run high‑volume decision tasks, challenging competitors such as TypeSafe’s Jev model.

item.title: Pathos AI partners with Bristol Myers Squibb and Tempus AI on Alzheimer drug development
item.description: Pathos AI announced a multi‑year collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb and Tempus AI, licensing a $55 million, five‑year dataset and applying its Pathos Foundry AI platform to accelerate Alzheimer’s and other neurological drug research. The deal coincides with a $237 million Series E round led by Bristol Myers, valuing Pathos at about $3 billion. It shows AI platforms being integrated into pharma pipelines to speed discovery and trial design for complex diseases.

item.title: Anthropic uses Claude to formally verify security properties in 123 open-source libraries
item.description: Anthropic and Theorem Labs reported that Claude generated machine‑checked formal proofs for security properties at the RISC‑V assembly level across 123 open‑source libraries, covering 239 fuzz‑test entry points. The effort produced about 180 million lines of Rocq proofs in a few weeks. It shows AI can dramatically speed up formal verification, making mathematical guarantees of code safety affordable for more projects.

item.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers over alleged leak of internal model designs
item.description: OpenAI terminated three safety researchers after an internal investigation said they leaked internal model designs via disappearing Signal chats; the researchers dispute the allegations. The incident highlights tensions between AI safety transparency and corporate security policies.

item.title: Swedish government offices ban ChatGPT and Claude, require Microsoft Copilot
item.description: Sweden's government ministries have prohibited staff from using ChatGPT and Claude on work computers. Employees must use Microsoft Copilot, the only AI tool approved for official use. The ban highlights growing concerns about AI security and data protection in public sector IT.

item.title: LTM launches BlueVerse Industrial AI Lab in Chennai
item.description: LTM opened its BlueVerse Industrial AI Lab in Chennai to let clients, partners and its teams develop, simulate and validate AI solutions for industrial operations before deployment. The lab provides a sandbox for testing AI in factories, helping firms move AI from pilots to production safely and faster.

item.title: Chariot launches real‑time speech model for 10 Indian languages
item.description: Chariot released Chariot‑1‑ASR Realtime, a speech‑to‑text model that supports Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia and Indian English, claiming lower error rates than competing systems across 79 public test sets. It shows a home‑grown model can outperform major providers in Indian language transcription, expanding options for developers and businesses needing accurate real‑time speech services.

item.title: OpenAI details new containment measures for frontier model training
item.description: OpenAI announced that it has added offline environments and high‑compute red‑teaming to its training and evaluation process to improve security. The changes are aimed at strengthening containment of frontier AI models. The tighter safeguards reduce the risk of accidental leaks or misuse of powerful AI systems.

item.title: Polish prime minister calls for deeper AI, digital and space cooperation with India
item.description: Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged stronger technology partnerships with India, proposing joint AI development, digital product creation and space technology projects, and invited Indian firms to joint ventures at the Global Investors Meet 2027. The push signals increased collaboration between two large economies on emerging AI and space technologies, affecting global market dynamics and research ecosystems.

item.title: Warp Sciences raises $215 million to build AI‑powered drug research labs
item.description: Warp Sciences, a startup founded by former OpenAI, Meta and other AI leaders, raised $215 million to create U.S. chemistry contract research labs that combine AI, robotics and chemists. The company will focus on lead optimisation through analogue synthesis for biotech and pharma clients. It shows AI and automation moving into wet‑lab drug discovery, potentially speeding up experiments and reducing reliance on overseas CROs.

item.title: Tech Mahindra partners with SpaceXSI to boost AI‑assisted software engineering
item.description: Tech Mahindra announced a collaboration with AI coding platform SpaceXSI to help global enterprises modernise legacy applications, accelerate delivery and improve developer productivity. The joint offering combines Tech Mahindra’s engineering and AI consulting with SpaceXSI’s AI‑powered development platform. It shows how AI tools are being integrated into enterprise software development to speed up projects while meeting security and compliance standards.
